title: Effects of a ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach on learners’ courseware project performances and perceptions
extended_summary:
This paper investigates whether integrating ChatGPT into a flipped learning environment can improve students’ project-based learning outcomes and perceptions. The study is motivated by a practical problem in flipped classrooms: teachers often cannot provide every learner with immediate, personalised guidance, especially during project-based activities that require ongoing feedback and scaffolding.

To address this, the author developed a ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach (ChatGPT-FLGA) using the ADDIE instructional design model. The system connected ChatGPT with Tencent QQ to provide an AI teacher that could offer instant feedback, reminders, and personalised guidance during a courseware design course. Students in the experimental condition learned with ChatGPT-FLGA, while the control group used a traditional flipped learning guiding approach without ChatGPT. The intervention lasted three weeks after an initial instruction period.

The participants were 81 pre-service teachers at a public normal university in mainland China, enrolled in a compulsory course on Modern Educational Technology. Quantitative measures included project performance and questionnaires on self-efficacy, learning attitudes, learning motivation, and creative thinking, supplemented by interviews with six students. Results showed that the ChatGPT-based approach significantly improved project performance, self-efficacy, learning attitudes, learning motivation, and creative thinking tendency compared with the control condition, suggesting that ChatGPT can strengthen personalised support in flipped, project-based learning.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental comparison study with a control group, pre/post measures, and ANCOVA controlling for baseline scores, which provides moderate causal evidence. However, it is not randomized at the individual level and the sample is small and from a single course/university, so there are important generalizability and internal validity concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports modest-to-medium positive effects, with partial η2 values ranging from 0.05 to 0.09 across outcomes. That places the impact in the green range because the effects are meaningful but not large, and they come from a narrow courseware-learning context rather than a broad K-12 population.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-based flipped learning guiding approach that provided instant personalized guidance, intelligent reminders, and human-mimicking conversational support during courseware project work in a flipped classroom.

finding.finding_summary: Students in the ChatGPT-FLGA group outperformed the control group on courseware project performance in a quasi-experiment with n=81 (experimental n=42, control n=39). The adjusted post-test mean was 89.93 vs 87.13, with ANCOVA showing a significant difference, F=8.32, p<0.05, partial η2=0.09, indicating a medium effect.
finding.measure: Courseware project performance rubric (instruction, science, technology, artistry, operability; max score 100)

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT-FLGA significantly improved students’ self-efficacy relative to the flipped-learning control condition in the same quasi-experiment (n=81; experimental n=42, control n=39). The adjusted mean self-efficacy score was 34.77 vs 33.14, with ANCOVA F=4.45, p<0.05, partial η2=0.05, a small effect.
finding.measure: Self-efficacy for Learning and Performance Scale (8 items, 5-point Likert)

finding.finding_summary: Learning attitudes were significantly higher for the ChatGPT-FLGA group than for the control group. The adjusted mean was 31.59 vs 29.91, with ANCOVA F=5.10, p<0.05, partial η2=0.06, suggesting a medium effect.

Learning motivation was significantly higher in the ChatGPT-FLGA condition than in the control group. The adjusted mean motivation score was 26.01 vs 25.14, with ANCOVA F=5.32, p=0.02, partial η2=0.06; intrinsic motivation was also significantly higher (adjusted mean 12.74 vs 12.12, F=7.38, p<0.05, partial η2=0.09), while extrinsic motivation showed no significant difference (F=1.01, p=0.32, partial η2=0.01).
finding.measure: Learning Motivation Scale (intrinsic and extrinsic motivation subscales)
finding.effect_size: partial η2=0.06 overall; partial η2=0.09 intrinsic; partial η2=0.01 extrinsic
finding.std_deviation: overall experimental SD=2.37; control SD=2.09; intrinsic experimental SD=1.50; control SD=1.27; extrinsic experimental SD=1.48; control SD=1.30

finding.finding_summary: Creative thinking tendency was significantly higher for students using ChatGPT-FLGA than for those in the flipped-learning control group. The adjusted mean was 19.07 vs 17.40, with ANCOVA F=6.85, p<0.05, partial η2=0.08, indicating a medium effect.
finding.measure: Creative Thinking Tendency Scale (5 items, 5-point Likert)
